classification.recommended_terminology: prime-double-prime certificate for a totient-driven affine-tail obstruction
classification.terminology_boundary: Finite difference, affine recurrence, eventual affinity, and noncollinearity are standard. Prime-double-prime certificate is a literal description of this witness, not a located theorem name.
nearest_prior_work: Martin (2006), Theorem 1, proves arbitrarily strong simultaneous inequalities for totient values on pairwise nonproportional affine forms, a much stronger global irregularity input than the three elementary values used here.

Coons (2010), Theorem 3.2, proves that the totient sequence is not k-regular for any k>=2; since eventually affine integer sequences are k-regular, it already excludes eventual affinity of the totient word by a more global method.
Neither source states the fixed-quotient endpoint cocycle or transfers totient non-affinity to the exact endpoint error coordinate.

primary_sources.title: Simultaneous inequalities among values of the Euler phi-function
primary_sources.author: Greg Martin
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Theorem 1 gives prescribed simultaneous totient-ratio inequalities by an arbitrary factor C on a positive-lower-density set for pairwise nonproportional positive affine forms.
primary_sources.supports: A strong established antecedent showing large, cofinal irregularity among totient values on affine forms.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The prime-double-prime determinant, endpoint cocycle, or eventual-affinity transfer theorem.

primary_sources.title: (Non)Automaticity of number theoretic functions
primary_sources.author: Michael Coons
primary_sources.venue: Journal de Théorie des Nombres de Bordeaux 22 (2010), 339-352
primary_sources.exact_anchor: Theorem 3.2 states that the Euler totient function is not k-regular for any k>=2.
primary_sources.supports: A stronger global complexity obstruction for the totient word; eventual affine integer sequences lie inside the k-regular class.
primary_sources.does_not_support: The endpoint-error sequence, a fixed quotient, or the card's exact all-basepoint recurrence consumer.

mechanism_comparison.transfer_core: Substitution of E_H=AH+B into E_(H+1)=2E_H+a_(H+1)-k forces a_(H+1)=-AH+A-B+k.
mechanism_comparison.arithmetic_core: For primes 2<p<q, the totient graph points at p,q,2p have affine determinant -p(q-p), hence are noncollinear and occur beyond every threshold.
mechanism_comparison.literature_relation: Known results establish much richer totient irregularity. The local theorem is valuable because it is an exact cheap consumer of the particular endpoint cocycle, not because it discovers that phi is irregular.
mechanism_comparison.exact_delta: A machine-checked cofinal contradiction for every basepoint and fixed quotient, paired with an honest statement of the nonlinear modes it does not touch.
